thread:
ash: re-opening the tenant networking tradeoff convo. we need a concrete pattern for private onboarding that balances: control-plane isolation, easy rollback, and predictable egress accounting. options on the table: agent-in-customer (outbound-only agent), regional gateway (our managed relay), or a lightweight tenant-bridge (transit account with per-tenant routes).

maria: +1. quick pros/cons from my POV: agent-in-customer = best for compliance & source-ip preservation; downside is customer infra burden and support overhead. regional gateway = fastest onboarding and centralized metrics but increases our egress footprint and can hide original src ip. tenant-bridge = middle ground but needs cross-account routing and adds single-account NAT costs.

zach: a few operational constraints to surface: cert lifecycle (customer vs us), rollback semantics, and partial-fallback (some routes to gateway, others to agent). also we should be explicit about what "agent" can and cannot do (no ENI creation, no route table writes). keep it drop-in.

oncall-bot: spike-run scheduled: onboard-patterns/bridge-vs-agent-vs-gateway. automated perf probes + heartbeat verification will run.

ash: thinking about rollback: we should design the CP routing layer so fallback is reversible and auditable. plan: agent registers ephemeral endpoint with TTL; CP routes by lookup table. if heartbeat absent, CP flips a per-route flag `use_path=gateway` and emits an event in the audit log. After TTL, CP rechecks. we need header semantics to make path explicit for debugging.

maria: I propose headers: `x-rw-path: agent|gateway|bridge` and `x-rw-path-reason: agent-unreachable|forced-fallback|manual` so support + logs can explain where traffic went. also include `x-rw-agent-version`.

zach: for partial-fallback config example (per-route):
```
connect:
  default: agent
  routes:
    - name: embeddings
      prefer: gateway
    - name: realtime-chat
      prefer: agent
  fallback:
    policy: auto
    ttl: 600s
    check_interval: 30s
```

ash: egress accounting note: tenant-bridge centralizes NAT which simplifies billing but shifts cost to one account. agent scatters egress which complicates metering. suggestion: if agent-mode, require customers to tag their NAT/gateway or provide flow logs; CP will ingest tags for cost attribution. if tenant opts out, we fall back to bridge/gateway. need finance input.

maria: security note: agent should authenticate with a one-time sigined bootstrap token and rotate keys frequently. prefer short-lived certs issued by CP with optional customer-managed root for enterprise. document threat model for agent compromise and how CP revokes endpoints.

zach: rollout strategy idea: GA defaults to gateway for self-serve. offer agent-mode for enterprise with onboarding checklist and a support-led rollout. tenant-bridge reserved for customers wanting centralized billing with explicit transit setup.

ash: action items: maria to draft header/audit schema + threat model (ETA Thu), zach to mock the per-route config and CP routing flags (ETA Fri), I'll coordinate finance for egress-tagging approach and schedule the spike. reconvene next week with findings.

maria: noted, taking headers/threat model.

ash: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
